source: segmentation (simulation with background replaced by white)

camera.evidence: plain white background (exactly 255), no background features; both objects keep constant y and constant pixel size -> no zoom/shake visible

boat.description: red/white fishing boat 'AH805' (red hull upper, dark purple/navy lower hull, white wheelhouse with mast), side view, bow pointing RIGHT; upper half of frame
boat.clipping: mast top cut by the top image edge in ALL frames (bbox y0=0), so the true height is unknown (>= 646 px); bow leaves right edge from frame 48; the mast leaves at frame 70
boat.reference_point: bbox centre x (frames 0-47); frames 48-72 = rigid hull template position + offset (exact for a rigid translating boat). ref_y = bbox centre y, which is biased by the clipped mast (vertical origin unknown; motion is purely horizontal)
boat.motion: stationary frames 0-1, then translates RIGHT at nearly constant ~17.9 px/frame (y constant)

shark.description: blue-grey shark with white belly, side view, head pointing LEFT; lower part of frame (y ~852-957), below the boat
shark.clipping: nose leaves the left edge at frame 59; only the tail fin remains at frame 72
shark.reference_point: bbox centre (frames 0-58); frames 59-72 = tail tip x1 - 139.5 px (approx, +-3 px because the tail flaps)
shark.motion: stationary frames 0-1, then swims LEFT with speed increasing steadily (~7.5-8 px/frame near frame 2-5 to ~15-16 px/frame near frame 55-58); y constant (~904)

static_objects: none (white background, no ground, no markings)

events.event: both objects at rest (frames 0 and 1 identical positions)
boat starts moving right (+17.5 px from frame 1) and shark starts moving left (-7.7 px)
boat bow reaches right image edge (x=1919)
shark nose reaches left image edge (x=0)
boat mast leaves frame at right
last frame: boat about half visible, shark only tail visible

relative_positions_frame0.note: boat ref_y is biased by mast clipping; keel bottom y=643, shark top y=853
